pages.title: Nervous system organization

concepts.label: Nervous system organization
concepts.detail: Nervous System -> CNS and PNS. CNS -> Brain (receives/processes sensory information; initiates responses; stores memories; generates thoughts/emotions) and Spinal cord (signals to/from brain; controls reflex activities). PNS -> Motor neurons (CNS to muscles/glands) and Sensory neurons (sensory organs to CNS). Motor neurons -> Somatic (voluntary movements) and Autonomic (involuntary responses). ANS -> Sympathetic (Fight or Flight), Parasympathetic (Rest or Digest).
concepts.rationale: Explicit mechanism,comparison,organ response or drug-specific relationship taught in the fourth chapter.

pages.title: Somatic and autonomic pathways

concepts.label: Somatic and autonomic pathways
concepts.detail: Somatic: one myelinated neuron from CNS releases acetylcholine at skeletal muscle. Sympathetic: myelinated preganglionic neuron releases acetylcholine at ganglion; unmyelinated postganglionic neuron releases norepinephrine. Adrenal medulla: preganglionic acetylcholine -> medulla -> epinephrine/norepinephrine in blood. Parasympathetic: preganglionic acetylcholine -> ganglion near target -> postganglionic acetylcholine. Autonomic effector labels: smooth muscle (blood vessel example), glands, cardiac muscle. Key distinguishes sympathetic and parasympathetic preganglionic/postganglionic fibers and myelination.
concepts.rationale: Explicit mechanism,comparison,organ response or drug-specific relationship taught in the fourth chapter.

pages.title: NE synthesis-storage-release-removal

concepts.label: NE synthesis-storage-release-removal
concepts.detail:
1.Synthesis of NE: tyrosine hydroxylation is rate-limiting; Na+ accompanies tyrosine uptake; tyrosine -> DOPA -> dopamine.
2.Uptake into storage vesicles: dopamine enters and becomes NE; vesicular NE protected from degradation; reserpine inhibits transport into vesicle.
3.Release: calcium influx triggers vesicle/cell-membrane fusion(exocytosis); guanethidine and bretylium block release.
4.Binding: neurotransmitter activates postsynaptic receptor; presynaptic receptor also drawn.
5.Removal: released NE rapidly taken into neuron; cocaine/imipramine inhibit reuptake.
6.Metabolism: COMT methylates NE; MAO oxidizes it. Inactive metabolites -> urine. Other labels: synaptic space, intracellular response, cell membrane, COMT.
concepts.rationale: Explicit mechanism,comparison,organ response or drug-specific relationship taught in the fourth chapter.
